_doc: DAY, NIGHT AND LAMPS (Phase 042). Seed: seeds/bigville_daynight.json (block R59). The sky is computed each tick from the clock, the calendar and the weather's cloud (domains/daynight.py); the consequences of light are switched by DAYNIGHT.enabled, which defaults OFF so the simple village is unchanged until it is switched on (a scenario or a test calls worlds/daynight.py switch_on). Sources: latitude_deg, summer_solstice_day, noon_hour, see_threshold, dark_sight_range, dark_work_fit, lamp, candle and oil figures are APPROX and are design choices, not measured; the seed gives no number for any of them. synodic_month_days 29.530588853 is the mean synodic month (Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, ch. 49). The declination formula is Cooper (1969). june solstice day 172 is the standard day of the year (non-leap). new_moon_day 0 is a choice: the founding clock starts at a new moon (APPROX). The consequence switches are: enabled (everything below the sky), travel_dark_factor (1.0 is the seed: travel in the dark costs nothing extra), and the lamplighter, who is appointed on switch-on and whose round is a backend choice. DAYNIGHT_LAMPS are street lamps at the market square's corners (offsets from the square's centre, TOWN_SQUARE_FIXTURES' convention). DAYNIGHT_MAJOR_ACTIONS are merged into MAJOR_ACTIONS by domains/world_affordances.py. Lamp and lantern art is not generated (follow-up); the lantern is not added (it would need an ITEMS row and art).

light.description: Light a lamp or a candle. Stand on a street lamp's cell to light the lamp: it is filled from the town's lamp oil first (what the reservoir can hold), and it burns until its oil is gone. Or hold a candle and name it to light the candle, which burns down. The world does not decide whether the light is needed or who may light it.

douse.description: Put out the lamp on the cell where you stand, or the candle you hold. A lamp keeps the oil it has left. The world does not decide whether it should be put out.
